localised_description: The Father of Darkness is served loudly, and the people are quiet.
The temples stand unattended and the sermons go unsaid.
The forges of Zharr-Naggrund answer to one voice, and it is his.
No hand guides the forges. Output slips and no one is blamed.
Every debt in the Dark Lands is written down, and he holds the book.
The books go unbalanced and the tribute arrives light.
The outer holds are watched, and the watchers are paid on time.
The marches keep themselves, badly and at their own expense.
He carries the Sorcerer-Prophets' word down the Tower, unaltered.
The Tower's word arrives late, and altered on the way.
He counts the work gangs, and the gangs know he counts them.
Uncounted, the work gangs move at their own pace.
What comes back from a battlefield is his to sort and his to sell.
The spoils are picked over by whoever reaches them first.
The black rock comes up faster when somebody is counting the carts.
The quarries run at the pace of the laziest overseer in them.
The roads out of Zharr are his, and they are quicker than they were.
The roads are unwatched, and the caravans take the long way round.
Brick and slag leave his kilns cheaper than anyone can explain.
The kilns burn on unwatched, and the bill still arrives.
The hobgoblin tribes that work the ash fields march cheap for whoever feeds them.
The ash fields go untended, and the hobgoblins want more to march.
His clerks know which door to knock on, and when.
The clerks knock on the wrong doors and are turned away.
He knows what a warrior costs, and he pays no more than that.
Every company is hired at whatever it asks for.
Raiding is an accounting exercise, and he keeps the account.
The raiders keep their own accounts, and most of the takings.
Nothing moves in Zharr-Naggrund that the Crown did not set moving.
localised_title: An Iron Grip on the Court

localised_description: The parties argue, and then they do as they are told.
The Crown leads the parties but cannot command them.
No decree passes without a bargain struck.
The parties rule. The Crown hears their decisions later.
No one rules Zharr-Naggrund. Its Sorcerer-Prophets sit in council.
The eldest priest rules in Hashut's name.
The priest-artificers rule from the forges.
Rank in the court is won in the field.
Fear holds the court as the chain holds the slave.
Everything in the Dark Lands has a price.
Keep the work gangs to their usual quotas.
More slaves are taken. The lash works them to death.
Feed the stock. Keep it alive. Take fewer slaves.
The stock pays for every forge's quota.
Burn what cannot be held, people and all.
The Crown collects its usual tithe.
More convoys use the roads. Vassals pay less tribute.
The Ledger takes more from each route. Cargo sells for less.
Supply the mines first. Convoys carry less.
Charter the convoy overseers. The other houses resent their privilege.
The priests keep the customary rites.
Feed Hashut's fires at the expense of building work.
Sell seats in the Tower. The priests withhold their favour.
Teach the Lore of Hashut widely, with less care.
License the Daemonsmiths. The priests resent their privilege.
Raise the customary levy.
The Hell-Forge needs no leave to work. Infantry pays the bill.
Keep the legions ready. The guns must wait.
Pursue the old grudge against the Dwarfs at the labourers' expense.
Supply the guns first. Shooters cost more to recruit.
The court's governor rules this province.
Your retainers answer for this province.
The temples take the province in hand and it grows for Hashut.
Forge-guild overseers run the province like a workshop floor.
The slavers work the province to the bone and account for every hour.
A garrison town under a soldier costs less to keep than it should.
Brokers keep the province's books, and the tribute arrives whole.
Tower clerks read everything that passes through, and pass it on.
The caravan men keep the roads open whatever the season.
The old clans hold it, and men come back to the muster faster.
The court's envoy keeps order here.
The court's envoy drives the forges here.
The court's envoy drives the mines harder.
The court's envoy keeps more Labourers alive.
He tends the clan shrines and settles disputes in their names.
The shrines stand unattended and the old names go unspoken.
The master smiths accept his judgement at the anvil.
The smiths dispute each other's work. No master settles the matter.
He makes each debtor pay what the hold is owed.
Unpaid debts gather in the hold's books.
He assigns the gate watch and keeps the garrison supplied.
The clans dispute who owes the gate watch.
Every wrong is written in his hand. From the next Age of Reckoning, fewer grudges need settling.
The Book goes unkept. From the next Age of Reckoning, more grudges need settling.
He keeps the old routes through the Underway clear.
Blocked tunnels force traders over the mountain passes.
He inspects each seam and accounts for every ore cart.
The mining clans quarrel over their claims.
He sees that spoils reach the hold's vaults.
Warriors take spoils before the hold receives its share.
His stonecutters waste little when they widen the halls.
The clans cannot agree whose halls to cut first.
He ensures each clan equips its warriors at a fair price.
Each clan asks its own price to send warriors.
Traders come for his ale and buy the hold's fine work beside it.
Poor ale drives traders away from the hold's wares.
He brings in enough grain to feed new households.
The holdfarms lack hands to feed new households.
He finds old designs the smiths can put to work.
The smiths repeat work from neglected old books.
He gathers supplies for the Grudge Settlers from each clan.
The Grudge Settlers must buy their own supplies.
Every clan accepts the king's authority.
localised_title: An Iron Grip on the Court

localised_description: The elders grumble but honour the king's decisions.
The king must hear the clans before he rules.
The clans bargain over each royal decree.
The clan elders decide matters without the king.
The king hears each clan elder before the council decides.
The priests judge the hold by the laws of its Ancestors.
The master smiths govern the hold between shifts at the forge.
The king leads the shield wall. Clan thanes must fight beside him.
An oath sworn in the hold is kept, or it is written down.
The king demands an account of every debt.
The clans work as their fathers worked.
Send more miners into the deep seams. The holdfarms lose hands.
The holdfarms get the hands they need before the mines.
Master smiths inspect every piece. Warriors wait for their equipment.
Widen the halls at the counting-houses' expense.
Each clan owes the king its customary tithe.
Clear the Underway for traders. Vassal holds owe less tribute.
Every hall pays the Reckoners. Traders pay at the gate and come less often.
Gather Oathgold for the hold. Repairs to the roads must wait.
Charter the holds to sell their craft. Warriors cost more to maintain.
The clans honour their Ancestors.
Supply Valaya's hearths before the loremasters' work.
Give the runesmiths leave to work. The shrines receive less.
Call clansmen from the holdfarms to study the old books.
The forge is licensed to work without the priests' leave.
Each clan sends its customary muster.
The king funds the Grudge Settlers from the counting-houses.
Guns come first. Infantry costs more to recruit.
Equip the clan hosts. The gun batteries must wait.
Engineers train the gun crews and Thunderers. Recruits cost more.
The king's governor answers for this province.
The king's retainers answer for this province.
The priests tend its clan shrines and keep its old grudges alive.
The Forgewrights collect Oathgold from the province's workshops.
The Deepdelvers weigh the spoils brought home by their warriors.
A thane knows what his clan needs to defend the hold.
The Reckoners collect every debt owed to the hold.
The Runesmiths put the hold's old lore to use.
The Underway Wardens clear safe routes beneath the mountains.
The Hearth Clans care for wounded warriors until they can march again.
The king's envoy settles disputes here.
The king's envoy collects Oathgold from the forges.
The king's envoy sees to the holdfarms.
The king's envoy reduces the cost of the clan muster.
